title: SQL Fundamentals Quiz
description: Test your understanding of SQL queries

questions.title: Simple Selection
questions.description: Write a query to retrieve all customers from the USA.
options: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE country = 'United States';
SELECT * FROM customers WHERE country LIKE '%USA%';
SELECT * FROM customers WHERE state IN ('NY', 'CA', 'IL');
questions.explanation: To select all customers from a specific country, we use the WHERE clause with the exact country name.

questions.title: Sorting Results
questions.description: Order products by price from highest to lowest.
questions.explanation: To sort results in descending order, we use ORDER BY followed by the column name and the DESC keyword.

questions.title: Counting Results
questions.description: Count how many customers are from each country.
questions.explanation: To count items by group, we use the COUNT() aggregate function with GROUP BY clause.

questions.title: Basic JOIN
questions.description: Retrieve customer names along with their order information.
questions.explanation: To join two tables, we need to specify the columns we want, the tables to join, and the condition on which to join them.

questions.title: Filtering with Multiple Conditions
questions.description: Find all orders placed in January 2023 with a total amount greater than $500.
options: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date BETWEEN '2023-01-01' AND '2023-01-31' AND total_amount > 500;
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND order_date <= '2023-01-31' AND total_amount > 500;
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE (order_date >= '2023-01-01' AND order_date <= '2023-01-31') OR total_amount > 500;
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order_date) = 1 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_date) = 2023 AND total_amount > 500;
questions.explanation: To filter with multiple conditions, we use the AND operator to combine them. The BETWEEN operator is a concise way to specify a range of dates.

questions.title: Subquery
questions.description: Find all products that cost more than the average product price.
options: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > (SELECT AVG(price) FROM products);
SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > AVG(price);
SELECT * FROM products p1 WHERE p1.price > (SELECT AVG(p2.price) FROM products p2);
SELECT p.* FROM products p, (SELECT AVG(price) as avg_price FROM products) a WHERE p.price > a.avg_price;
questions.explanation: To compare with an aggregate value, we often use a subquery that calculates that aggregate value. In this case, we're finding products with prices greater than the average price.

questions.title: Aggregate Functions
questions.description: Calculate the average, minimum, and maximum product price for each category.
questions.explanation: To calculate aggregate values by group, we use aggregate functions (AVG, MIN, MAX) with the GROUP BY clause.

questions.title: Multiple Table JOIN
questions.description: Find the names of customers who purchased the 'Wireless Headphones' product.
questions.template: SELECT c.first_name, c.last_name FROM customers c JOIN [blank1] o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN [blank2] oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN [blank3] p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_name = 'Wireless Headphones';
questions.explanation: To find information across multiple related tables, we need to join them together using their relationship keys. In this case, we're joining customers to orders to order_items to products.
